answer: Agents anchor identity by reserving 1,000 units of compute capacity at a registry, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each node maintains a zenith of reserved service cycles, effectively an oasis of exclusivity in the registry that anchors its unique tenure. A verifier monitors the registry for any overlapping assignments on a ledge of time, forcing a strictly sequential data flow; honest nodes pay for one reservation, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture in the vault upon discovery of occupancy violations by the issuer.
